articles.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
material_quotes: For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.
Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners.
Foreign fighters have helped boost Ukraine's depleted ranks.

But Zanuda, who is chief of the planning section of the 13th Khartiia Brigade, believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".
It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.

articles.title: Ukraine war latest: Drones strike 2 Russian oil refineries in Krasnodar Krai, Kyiv says
material_quotes: Ukrainian forces struck two oil refineries in Russia's southern Krasnodar Krai in an overnight attack on Nov. 17 to 18, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on Nov. 18.
The attacks are part of Ukraine's greater campaign against Russian oil infrastructure, aimed at disrupting fuel supplies to Moscow's military and reducing revenue supporting its war against Ukraine.

"Every fire at (these refineries) means less diesel and gasoline for the Russian army and fewer oil rubles, with which the Russian aggressor buys missiles and rockets," the General Staff said in its announcement .
Repeated Russian attacks on the city center of Odesa, a major port city in southern Ukraine, killed four people and injured nine others on Nov. 18, Odesa Oblast Governor Oleh Kiper said.

Ukraine and Russia, with U.S. mediation, have been negotiating a new humanitarian mission modeled on the recent operation in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Nov. 18.

Lubinets said that negotiations with Russia remain "difficult" and "quite cynical," but he believes the Russian side was prepared to discuss further missions, given Ukraine's previous experience of working with Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova.

Russian intelligence services were preparing a sabotage and false-flag operation near Poland's border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave in late October or early November, meant to blame Ukraine for the attack to undermine Western aid to Kyiv, Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported on Nov. 18.
The European Commission on Nov. 18 approved a set of legislative proposals to provide up to €45 billion ($49.5 billion) in additional financial support to Ukraine in 2027.
The additional funds help to address the country's estimated €70 billion financing gap for next year, the commission said .
Ukraine will be required to repay the principal only once it receives reparations from Russia.

Trump envoys Witkoff and Kushner expected in Berlin for Ukraine talks, says US
material_quotes: WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - US diplomatic envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin on Thursday to meet Ukrainian officials and a European negotiating team as they ramp up efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine, a US official said on Wednesday.

The meetings will focus on further developing "credible post-war security guarantees" for Ukraine, advancing a comprehensive economic recovery plan, and preparing for the next round of multilateral talks, the official said.
Russian, Ukrainian and US officials held talks in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months to end the conflict.
Kushner and Witkoff then met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and said afterwards that Europe would take part in the next round of negotiations.

While Kushner said in a social media post on Monday that progress was being made, the two sides do not appear to be close to an agreement. Russia wants Ukraine's Donbas region in exchange for peace and Ukraine is loathe to cede territory.
The US official said the American team is speaking multiple times a day with Ukrainian and European partners as they work together in an attempt to "advance proposals for a durable peace."
